hazardRates.definition: A pandemic of roughly COVID-19 scale reaching the household's city: a novel transmissible agent with infection fatality around 0.1-1% concentrated in the old, several million to a few tens of millions of deaths worldwide, and months of partial closure of schools, workplaces and some supply lines. Natural, accidental or deliberate.

baseline.basis: Historical-statistics range with AI removed. Low end from Marani et al. 2021 (PNAS), COVID-like intensity about 38% per lifetime, which is about 0.6%/yr over an 80-year life (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8536331/, read in research/step2/base-rates.md). High end from Metabiota via CGD, COVID-scale 2.5-3.3%/yr (https://www.cgdev.org/blog/the-next-pandemic-could-come-soon-and-be-deadlier). Mid splits them; Marani also argue spillover drivers may raise the rate up to threefold.

now.basis: Baseline plus a human-caused component. FRI 2025 experts put a human-caused epidemic killing >100,000 at 0.3%/yr baseline, rising to 1.5%/yr conditional on the virology-troubleshooting threshold that has since been met (https://forecastingresearch.org/ai-enabled-biorisk). I take the current human-caused >100k rate as 0.8%/yr (shaded below 1.5% because the one large wet-lab RCT found no novice uplift) and assume about 30% of such events reach COVID scale, giving +0.24 pp. The lo is the sceptic's view (Narayanan and Kapoor; RAND 2024; Active Site RCT) that AI adds nothing measurable at this scale.

transition.basis: Five years from AGI. Human-caused >100k-death epidemics taken at about 6%/yr (FRI's combined-capability conditional was already 2.3% expert / 3% superforecaster for 2026-era evals, and AGI exceeds all five thresholds), of which about 30% reach COVID scale, so about +1.8 pp; natural rate falls slightly as detection improves. lo is the view that mandatory synthesis screening plus strong model safeguards hold the increase near zero, which FRI found pulls the expert conditional from 1.25% back to 0.4%. hi reflects Esvelt and Amodei on the attack-defence asymmetry.

after.basis: Conditional on the transition being survived, which correlates with defences and governance having worked. Pathogen-agnostic defences (far-UVC, building-level air treatment), metagenomic surveillance and days-to-weeks vaccines would make a COVID-scale household disruption rare, so mid is about a quarter of baseline. hi is the world where open-weight biological design tools proliferated: the International AI Safety Report 2026 reports 23% of top-performing biological AI tools have high misuse potential, 61.5% of those fully open source, and only 3% of 375 surveyed tools carry any safeguards.

hazardRates.mechanism: At COVID scale AI barely moves the number: the natural spillover rate dominates, and a deliberate or accidental release of a COVID-severity agent is a small addition to it. AI's larger effect here is on the other side, shortening the time from detection to a vaccine and improving surveillance, which shortens the household's window rather than changing whether it opens.

survivableShare.basis: A COVID-scale pandemic is survivable by construction: COVID-19 itself killed roughly 0.1% of the world population over three years. Essentially all of this probability is a world in which household stocks, masks and an isolation plan matter.

evidence.claim: Median expert annual risk of a human-caused epidemic causing >=100,000 deaths or >=$1 trillion damage was 0.3% (IQR 0.01-2%); superforecasters 0.38% (IQR 0.1-1.21%)
Metabiota: COVID-scale pandemic 2.5-3.3% per year, 47-57% within 25 years
Marani et al.: COVID-like intensity about 38% per lifetime; 1918-intensity 0.27-1.9%/yr; rate may rise up to threefold
A 153-participant, 8-week randomised wet-lab trial found LLM access produced no significant effect on end-to-end success for novices across the three core tasks

hazardRates.notes: Location 'all'. Buenos Aires differs in two ways the model cares about: the Southern Hemisphere historically gets a few extra weeks of warning (COVID-19 reached Argentina about two months after Western Europe), which raises the chance an unprepared household can still buy staples; against that, imported pharmaceuticals and a thinner retail inventory make the medication window longer. Neither changes the annual probability enough to justify a separate entry.

hazardRates.definition: A pandemic far worse than COVID-19 reaching the household's city: infection fatality of roughly several percent or more for an unprotected adult of any age, not concentrated in the elderly, at least 1918-scale in relative mortality, with months of self-imposed or ordered isolation. Natural, accidental (including from AI-accelerated laboratory research) or deliberately engineered.

baseline.basis: Natural rate with AI removed. Upper anchor: Marani et al. 2021 put a 1918-intensity event at 0.27-1.9%/yr (mean recurrence about 400 years, i.e. 0.25%/yr). Lower anchor: XPT forecasters are far below that. Superforecasters gave 3.63% and biorisk experts 8.14% for a non-engineered pathogen killing >1% of the population in five years, by 2100, which annualises to about 0.05% and 0.11%/yr (https://forum-bots.effectivealtruism.org/posts/9ddheDChiMhveCfSw). Mid of 0.3% sits between the statistical fit and the forecasters, and includes a small pre-LLM human-caused component (about 0.03%/yr).

now.basis: Baseline 0.3% plus a human-caused severe component. FRI's expert median for a human-caused >=100,000-death epidemic rises from 0.3% to 1.5%/yr conditional on LLMs matching the top team of five expert virologist teams on the VCT, a threshold the same team's baselining study found o3 had already crossed; 0.84% conditional on the long-form biothreat threshold, which they judge likely met. I take the present >=100k human-caused rate as 0.8%/yr and assume about 12% of such events reach several-percent-fatality pandemic severity, giving +0.10 pp; so mid is about 1.5x baseline. lo is the careful sceptic (RAND 2024 red-team: no statistically significant difference in plan viability; Active Site RCT: no novice uplift; Ben Ouagrham-Gormley on tacit knowledge) combined with the XPT-style low natural rate. hi is the concerned view (FRI experts' 1.5% taken at face value with a 30% severe share, plus Anthropic's statement that for current models 'the evidence is no longer certain').

transition.basis: Per year over the five years from AGI. AGI exceeds all five FRI capability thresholds, including the human-uplift ones that are the actual bottleneck; FRI's combined-capability conditional was already 2.3% (expert) / 3% (superforecaster) on 2026-era evals. I take the human-caused >=100k rate at about 6%/yr with a 20% severe share (deliberate releases in this period are selected for severity), about 1.2 pp, plus roughly 0.2 pp each from natural events and from accidents in vastly accelerated wet-lab research. Cross-check: 1.5%/yr is about 7% over five years, inside the 3-10% that Metaculus shows for an engineered pandemic infecting a billion people within five years of AGI. lo is Narayanan and Kapoor plus FRI's mitigation result (strict anti-jailbreak safeguards and mandatory nucleic-acid screening pulled the expert conditional from 1.25% back to 0.4%, near baseline). hi is Esvelt, Amodei and the AI 2027 race branch.

after.basis: Conditional on no existential catastrophe, which is itself evidence that defences and governance held. Mature pathogen-agnostic defence (far-UVC and building air treatment, universal metagenomic surveillance, days-to-weeks countermeasures, enforced synthesis screening and verified-access model programmes) plausibly cuts the severe rate well below the historical natural rate; Michael Dickens' framing is that AI raises biological risk until it is powerful enough to shut the danger down. hi is the persistent-offence world: proliferated open-weight biological design tools and feasible mirror life, which the 2024 Science warning put at one to a few decades away and which AI could bring forward.

hazardRates.mechanism: AI removes the two barriers that have kept severe engineered pandemics rare: the specialist knowledge to design and troubleshoot a pathogen, and the tacit laboratory skill to build one. Frontier models already match top virologist teams on troubleshooting, and labs now ship with safeguards because they cannot rule out meaningful assistance to novices; the remaining wet-lab barrier is the one AGI-era automated laboratories and biological design tools are most likely to dissolve. AI also accelerates the legitimate research that leaks, and it accelerates state programmes. Against this, the same systems strengthen synthesis screening, surveillance and countermeasure design, and FRI's experts say those mitigations can pull most of the increase back.

survivableShare.basis: XPT medians imply extinction (population below 5,000) from an engineered pathogen is 0.01% (superforecasters) to 1% (biorisk experts), against 0.8% to 3% for a catastrophe killing >=10% of humanity: an extinction-to-catastrophe ratio of about 1% to 33%. 'pandemicSevere' is a lower bar than the 10% catastrophe, so the unsurvivable share of it is smaller still. I then subtract two transition-specific branches in which no household measure helps: a takeover scenario in which an AI releases pathogens deliberately to eliminate humans (AI 2027's race ending has 'the few survivors (e.g. preppers in bunkers, sailors on submarines)' killed by drones), and mirror life, which Amodei describes as potentially 'destroying all life on earth'. Period-weighted: about 0.97 for baseline and now, about 0.70 during the transition, about 0.8 after.

evidence.claim: Expert median annual risk of a human-caused epidemic causing >=100,000 deaths rose from 0.3% baseline to 1.5% conditional on LLMs matching the top of five expert virologist teams on the VCT, and to 2.3% on three capabilities combined; superforecasters 0.38% to 0.7% and 3%. A baselining study then found o3 already performs comparably to the top team; the median respondent had expected this only after 2030

Experts' conditional risk fell from 1.25% to 0.4%, near their baseline, given proprietary models with strict anti-jailbreaking safeguards and legally mandatory synthetic nucleic acid screening; screening alone removed 0.35 percentage points

XPT: a genetically engineered pathogen killing >1% of the population in five years, by 2100 — superforecaster median 4%, biorisk expert median 10.25%; catastrophe (>=10% of humanity) 0.8% and 3%; extinction (population <5,000) 0.01% and 1%

Anthropic: evaluations 'clearly showed' Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4.5 were 'well below the threshold where they could meaningfully assist a sophisticated user', but for current models 'the evidence is no longer certain, and we cannot make that same assurance'
Anthropic says assessments show Claude Fable 5 'could provide significant uplift' to a malicious actor and that the model 'can now outperform experts on some highly complex biological tasks'

A 153-novice randomised wet-lab trial costing $1.9M found no significant end-to-end effect of LLM access across three core tasks, though models helped at individual steps; METR cautions it covers one threat model and 'cannot be the sole basis for risk assessment'
RAND red-team study found 'no statistically significant difference in the viability of plans' generated with or without LLM assistance

80,000 Hours, updated October 2026: XPT puts a genetically engineered pathogen killing over 1% of the population by 2100 at 4-10%; Ord's Precipice gives about 3% existential risk from engineered pandemics by 2120

hazardRates.notes: How an AI-enabled severe pandemic differs from a natural one, in the model's terms. (1) Warning time collapses. A natural pandemic is seeded once and announces itself abroad: COVID-19 gave most households six to ten weeks between the first foreign reports and local closure, which is why unprepared households could still buy staples and even respirators. A deliberate release can be seeded in many cities at once, so detection and local spread coincide; warningDays falls from roughly 30-60 to 0-7 and lateBuy for specialty items (respirators, filters) falls close to zero. This is the single largest change for the ranking: it is what makes pre-purchase of air protection worth far more than the probability shift alone. (2) Multiple or sequential agents. Esvelt's argument is that an attacker able to release one pathogen can release several, and that 'a reactive vaccine strategy is nearly useless against anyone capable of continually releasing new pandemics'. The model should treat the window length distribution as having a much fatter tail: repeated waves rather than one, with no terminal countermeasure. (3) Duration. COVID-scale acute scarcity lasted two to eight weeks; a several-percent-fatality agent plausibly means one to six months during which the household chooses to stay in, repeated. (4) Supply chains. At 0.5% IFR, workers kept working. At several percent across ages, absenteeism in trucking, ports, water treatment and pharmacy is the binding constraint, so the food, medication and payments windows all lengthen, and the water window can open at all (it essentially did not in COVID). (5) Countermeasures. Natural agents get a vaccine in about a year today and governments target 100 days; an engineered immune-evasive agent may get none, so the household cannot assume the window ends. (6) Leaving stops helping. leave.feasible should be low and earliestDay late, because the destination is infected too and travel is itself the exposure; this is the opposite of a storm or a wildfire. (7) Distinct sources worth keeping separate: lone-actor misuse (the FRI threshold story), state programmes (Anthropic's September 2026 report describes work it assessed as part of a state-supported programme, and US officials have alleged AI-accelerated Chinese military-civilian work), and accidents in AI-accelerated research (Dickens' point that AI compresses the timeline to dangerous knowledge whether or not anyone misuses a model). Only the first is addressed by model safeguards, which is why the lo ends of the transition and after rates should not be read as 'safeguards solve it'.

views.who: Forecasting Research Institute (Williams, Righetti, Rosenberg, ... Karger, Tetlock), 46 biosecurity/biology experts and 22 superforecasters
views.claim: Median expert: 0.3% annual probability that a human-caused pathogen release in 2028 causes >=100,000 excess deaths or $1 trillion damage within 3 years (IQR 0.01-2%). Superforecaster median 0.38% (IQR 0.1-1.21%).

views.who: Forecasting Research Institute (same study)
views.claim: Conditional on LLMs matching or outperforming the top of five expert virologist teams on the Virology Capabilities Test, the expert median rises to 1.5% and the superforecaster median to 0.7%. Conditional on an RCT showing LLMs enable 50% of non-experts to synthesise influenza, 1.25% (experts) and 1.5% (superforecasters). Conditional on three capabilities together, 2.3% and 3%.

views.who: Forecasting Research Institute (same study)
views.claim: Participants badly underestimated the pace: the median expert gave the VCT top-team threshold 14% by 2026 with a most likely date of 2030 (superforecasters 2% and 2034), yet a baselining study with SecureBio found OpenAI's o3 already comparable to the top team. Median expected dates for the other thresholds were 2030-2040.

views.who: Forecasting Research Institute (same study)
views.claim: Mitigations pull the increase back: in the '50% of non-experts synthesise influenza' scenario, proprietary models with strict anti-jailbreaking measures plus legally mandatory synthetic nucleic acid screening cut the expert median from 1.25% to 0.4%. Screening alone removed 0.35 percentage points for the median expert, 0.14 for the median superforecaster.

views.who: Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament (FRI, 2022; 169 forecasters, 89 superforecasters)
views.claim: Genetically engineered pathogen killing >1% of the population in a five-year period, by 2100: superforecaster median 4%, biorisk expert median 10.25%. Non-engineered: 3.63% and 8.14%. The >=10%-of-humanity and extinction questions were kept out of the main tournament for information-hazard reasons and asked in a separate survey: engineered catastrophe 0.8% (superforecasters) and 3% (experts); engineered extinction, population below 5,000, 0.01% and 1%.

views.who: Scott Alexander, summarising the XPT
views.claim: Across all causes, superforecasters put extinction by 2100 at about 1% and experts about 6%; 'catastrophe' meant killing >10% of the population within five years and 'extinction' meant reducing population below 5,000.

views.who: 80,000 Hours problem profile 'Preventing catastrophic pandemics' (updated 16 October 2026)
views.claim: Calls the XPT 'perhaps the best estimates': catastrophe (10%+ of humanity) from pathogens by 2100 about 1-3%, extinction between 1 in 50,000 and 1 in 100. Cites Ord's Precipice at about 3% existential risk from engineered pandemics by 2120, against Millett and Snyder-Beattie at 0.00019%/yr. Judges catastrophic pandemics 'somewhat less pressing than threats stemming from advanced AI systems' but 'probably not massively less'.

views.who: Anthropic, threat intelligence report, September 2026
views.claim: Five cases of actors using Claude in ways that could support biological weapons development between December 2025 and August 2026, including gain-of-function work on chikungunya and mammalian adaptation of H5 avian influenza, one assessed as part of a state-supported programme. Evaluations 'clearly showed' Opus 4 and Sonnet 4.5 were 'well below the threshold where they could meaningfully assist a sophisticated user'; for current models 'the evidence is no longer certain, and we cannot make that same assurance'.

views.who: Anthropic, 'Improving Fable 5's biology safeguards' (7 August 2026)
views.claim: Fable 5 'can now outperform experts on some highly complex biological tasks and provide operational support on others' and 'could provide significant uplift' to a malicious actor. At launch nearly all biology queries were routed to a weaker fallback model; retraining the classifier cut biology-related fallbacks by about 85%. Anthropic says it is 'committed to closing that gap through trusted access pathways for frontier biology capabilities'.

views.who: Dario Amodei, 'The Adolescence of Technology' (January 2026)
views.claim: Models are 'likely now approaching the point where, without safeguards, they could be useful in enabling someone', perhaps 'doubling or tripling the likelihood of success'; 'added up across millions of people and a few years of time, I think there is a serious risk of a major attack', and some agents 'could cause millions of deaths'. 'There is an asymmetry between attack and defense in biology', so 'our expectations on the defensive side should be limited' and 'preventative safeguards will be our main line of defense'. Cites the 2024 report that mirror bacteria 'could plausibly be created in the next one to few decades' and could in the worst case destroy all life on earth. Puts powerful AI at 'as little as 1-2 years away'.

views.who: Kevin Esvelt (MIT Media Lab), UnHerd, 9 October 2026
views.claim: A model able to help a skilled attacker design immune-evasive pathogens faster than defences adapt is 'likely to be trained within a few years'; 'AI is democratising competence'; 'a reactive vaccine strategy is nearly useless against anyone capable of continually releasing new pandemics'. Recommends non-specific physical defences — stockpiled protective equipment that 'can filter out viruses and bacteria before they're inhaled', far-UVC and glycol vapours that 'can suppress airborne pathogens without first needing to recognise them' — plus legally required synthesis screening. 'Even a small annual probability adds up.'

views.who: Kevin Esvelt, 'Delay, Detect, Defend' (GCSP Geneva Paper 29/22)
views.claim: Within about a decade, tens of thousands of skilled individuals will be able to access the information needed to single-handedly cause new pandemics; today only one or two hundred could assemble a large poxvirus such as variola.

views.who: Active Site RCT, reported by Luca Righetti (METR), February 2026
views.claim: 153 novices, randomised to LLM access or internet only, performed wet-lab tasks over 8 weeks at a cost of $1.9M. AI 'did not produce a significant effect on end-to-end success across the three core tasks together', though there were 'signs of helpfulness at individual steps'. METR cautions that RCTs 'measure the combined effect' of model capability and user skill and 'cannot be the sole basis for risk assessment'.

views.who: RAND (Mouton, Lucas, Guest), red-team study, January 2024
views.claim: Teams role-playing non-state actors planned biological attacks with and without LLM access; there was 'no statistically significant difference in the viability of plans'. Attack planning 'currently lies beyond the capability frontier of LLMs as assistive tools'.

views.who: RAND (Roger Brent and Greg McKelvey Jr.), 'Contemporary Foundation AI Models Increase Biological Weapons Risk', 31 December 2025
views.claim: Three 2024 models gave accurate, usable guidance on recovering a live poliovirus from a construct built from commercially obtained synthetic DNA; current safety assessments relying on tacit-knowledge arguments and weak benchmarks 'may create a false sense of security'; 'models are already capable of guiding motivated users to develop biological weapons'.

views.who: Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor, 'AI as Normal Technology'
views.claim: Bioterrorism is real but 'this does not make bioterror an AI risk — any more than it is an internet risk'. 'Defenses must focus on the downstream attack surfaces'; concerns about biological risk 'are best addressed at the procurement and screening stages'; and 'giving defenders access to powerful AI tools often improves the offense-defense balance in their favor'.

views.who: Sonia Ben Ouagrham-Gormley (George Mason), Georgetown Journal of International Affairs, 27 August 2026
views.claim: Rejects the de-skilling narrative: 'explicit information is an incomplete representation of its authors' knowledge', non-experts cannot spot critical errors in AI-generated protocols, and Soviet experience shows that even with full protocols and samples Stepnogorsk needed about three further years of experimentation. Policy should target expertise acquisition and system integration, not technology access.

views.who: Allison Berke (RAND) and David Relman (Stanford), quoted in the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, 27 July 2026
views.claim: Berke sees 'a very, very small chance' of AI causing a biological crisis, because cloud labs cannot yet autonomously make a transmissible virus; a cheap benchtop synthesiser would change her view. Relman found an unrestricted model 'helpful, but not revolutionary' and mainly useful to people already familiar with biology, but says jailbreaking is 'absolutely doable' and expects 'a much more risky circumstance' within a year. Between 1970 and 2019 the Global Terrorism Database recorded over 200,000 attacks, 'just a few dozen' involving biological agents.

views.who: Wendy Barclay and colleagues (Imperial College London), quoted in MIT Technology Review, 18 September 2026
views.claim: AI tools are not yet good enough to fully develop biological weapons, and testing new pathogens still requires difficult, time-consuming human work; the greater near-term pandemic risk comes from circulating pathogens such as H5N1 rather than engineered agents. In the same piece Esvelt says a model 'disclosed a novel form of bioweapon that I hadn't realized was possible', and Evan Hubinger (Anthropic) says he personally puts the chance of AI being catastrophic at '>10% within the next decade'.

views.who: International AI Safety Report 2026 (over 100 contributors; biological and chemical risks from p. 64), as summarised by Stephen Turner, 3 February 2026
views.claim: Leading systems now match or exceed expert-level performance on benchmarks for weapons-relevant biological knowledge (o3 reportedly outperforms 94% of domain experts at troubleshooting virology protocols); OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind all shipped models with heightened safeguards because they could not rule out meaningful assistance to novices; substantial uncertainty remains about material barriers. 23% of the highest-performing biological AI tools have high misuse potential, 61.5% of those are fully open source, and only 3% of 375 surveyed tools carry any safeguards.

views.who: Alvin Ånestrand, 'AI and biological risk: forecasting key capability thresholds' (2 October 2025)
views.claim: Maps FRI's scenarios onto Anthropic's CBRN-3/CBRN-4 and OpenAI's High/Critical, and gives median timelines: basic support for experts already passed, basic support for novices late 2025, advanced support for experts late 2026, advanced support for novices early 2028. Reports Claude Opus 4 at 2.53x uplift in Anthropic's trial against a 5x threshold, and o3 at 43.8% on the VCT versus 22.1% for experts in their own domains.

views.who: AI Futures Project (Kokotajlo, Lifland, Dean; Alexander), AI 2027
views.claim: In the scenario, Agent-1 in late 2025 'could offer substantial help to terrorists designing bioweapons'; by July 2027 a fine-tuned Agent-3-mini will 'provide detailed instructions for human amateurs designing a bioweapon'; and in the race ending, mid-2030, 'the AI releases a dozen quiet-spreading biological weapons in major cities', after which 'the few survivors (e.g. preppers in bunkers, sailors on submarines) are mopped up by drones'.

views.who: AI Futures Project, Q1 2026 and Q2.5 2026 timelines updates
views.claim: April 2026: Kokotajlo's median for the Automated Coder moved from late 2029 to mid-2028 and Lifland's from early 2032 to mid-2030, with AGI medians about 1.5 years sooner. August 2026: timelines 'got slightly shorter'; reality is running at 'roughly 70-90% the speed of AI 2027'; Halstead gives 60% on the Automated Coder by January 2030 and 80% by January 2035.

views.who: Michael Dickens, 'AI will make biological extinction risks worse before it makes them better' (29 June 2026)
views.claim: AI raises biological risk first because 'AI accelerates the rate of scientific progress' toward extinction-level knowledge whether or not models are misused; if AI compresses a century of progress into a decade, capability that would have arrived around 2126 could arrive by 2036. He sees no route to eliminating biological existential risk short of an ASI controlling all science.

views.who: Alex Tabarrok, 'Pandemic Preparation is AI Safety' (17 September 2026)
views.claim: 'AI surely increases pandemic risks' and 'we should accept that AI will magnify the power of small groups'; but 'faster science does not automatically mean faster defense', because institutions must still turn discoveries into deployed countermeasures. Recommends banked capacity: wastewater surveillance, pre-developed vaccine libraries, pre-planned human challenge trials, a pandemic trust fund.

views.who: Coefficient Giving (formerly Open Philanthropy), biosecurity request for proposals, 2026
views.claim: Expects to direct over $100 million to biosecurity in 2026 across four priorities: transmission suppression (PPE stockpiles, air filters, disinfectant vapours), technical safeguards and governance at the AI-biology intersection (synthesis screening, misuse classifiers), policy and advocacy including mirror bacteria, and field-building. Rationale: AI could lower barriers for actors seeking novel biological weapons, and capable AI systems may themselves leverage biotechnology harmfully.

views.claim: Search snapshots show roughly 3-10% for 'by five years after AGI, will an engineered pandemic have infected one billion people?' (about 32 forecasters), about 25% for synthetic biological weapons infecting 100 people by 2030, and about 5% for a novel pathogen killing over 25 million people between 2022 and 2031.

views.who: Adamala et al., 'Confronting risks of mirror life', Science, 20 December 2024 (38-scientist working group)

Subsequent assessments (UN scientific advisory board, March 2026; WHO Q&A, February 2026) put the range at 10-30 years and say mirror bacteria should not be created absent compelling evidence of safety.

openQuestions: The single largest lever on pandemicSevere is the share of human-caused epidemics killing >=100,000 that go on to reach several-percent fatality across ages. I use 12% now and 20% during the transition, from a judgement about the heavy tail of outbreak sizes, not from a fitted distribution. Someone should fit this to Marani's power law or to an explicit engineered-release model; a factor of three here moves the transition rate by a factor of three.

Marani's statistical rate for 1918-intensity events (0.27-1.9%/yr) is five to twenty times the XPT forecasters' implied rate for a natural pathogen killing >1% of the population. The gap is not reconciled anywhere I could find, and it drives the whole baseline range.

Whether 'pandemicSevere' should be defined by fatality ratio (as here) or by total deaths. The two give different answers for a severe but contained outbreak, and the item side of the model (respirators, isolation plan) cares about the former.
No source quantifies the lab-accident rate conditional on AI-accelerated research volume. I assign roughly 0.2 pp/yr during the transition on judgement alone.

The model's survivableShare for pandemicSevere depends on how much of the transition-period probability is AI-takeover-driven. That belongs to whoever has the takeover assignment; if their number differs from my implicit 20-30% during the transition, this should be reconciled.
Whether the model should let an AI-enabled pandemic open a water window at all. I argue it can (treatment-plant absenteeism) where COVID did not, but no source supports a number.
